rows.answer: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources [3]. By incorporating an information-retrieval mechanism, RAG allows models to access and utilize additional data beyond their original training set [2]. The technique first has LLMs refer to a specified set of documents before responding to user queries, which supplements information from the model's pre-existing training data [3].

The data that RAG references is typically converted into LLM embeddings, which are numerical representations in the form of a large vector space [2]. This process can be used on unstructured, semi-structured, or structured data, such as knowledge graphs [2]. Additionally, chunking involves various strategies for breaking up the data into vectors so that the retriever can find details within it [1][3]. Finally, these embeddings are stored in a vector database to allow for document retrieval [2].
Hybrid vector approaches combine dense vector representations with sparse one-hot vectors [4].
RAG can be used on unstructured (usually text), semi-structured, or structured data, such as knowledge graphs [2].
